newsitem.title: USA: Heart surgeons cool to new devices - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: Heart surgeons cool to new devices - Barron's.

text.p: Heart surgeons are cool to surgical devices and techniques proposed by Heartport and CardioThoracic Systems, Barron's reported.
Both companies offer techniques for minimally invasive heart surgery, the financial weekly said.

Heartport developed a system to stop a heart from beating while it is being operated on, the paper said. Heartport's system involves using a machine to pump blood while the heart is stopped, Barron's said.
CardioThoracic devised a coronary bypass system for doctors operating on a beating heart, Barron's said.
Dr. Valavanur Subramanian, CardioThoracic's scientific advisor, told Barron's that 50 percent of heart surgeries performed would be done using the beating heart method in five or six years.
Other surgeons, however, told the paper the beating-heart approach is good in only about five percent of operations.
Surgeons were also critical of Heartport, since the 250 operations used to test its technique are not large enough of a sample to back up the company's claims, the paper said.
CardioThoracic Systems and Heartport were not immediately available for comment.
